title: Prospective quality of life study in patients with Wilson Disease
summary: Wilson's disease is a rare genetic disorder in which copper accumulates in organs, especially the liver and the brain. The quality of life of patients with Wilson's disease can be significantly affected by the physical and psychological consequences of the illness. Early diagnosis and treatment, usually with medications to reduce copper levels, can help improve quality of life. Regular check-ups are important to monitor the progression of the disease and its impact on quality of life. Quality of life assessments for patients with Wilson's disease often include questionnaires and tools that capture various areas of life, such as physical health, cognitive function, emotional stability, and social participation. Symptoms like tremor, motor disorders, fatigue, and depression, as well as the presence of cirrhosis, can strongly influence daily life and overall life satisfaction. The quality of life of patients with Wilson's disease can be significantly impacted by the physical and psychological effects of the condition. This may encompass various aspects of life. So far, there have been few studies on quality of life in Wilson's disease. The planned study aims to prospectively investigate the quality of life in patients with Wilson's disease using various questionnaires and correlate the findings with the patient's relevant clinical data. Additionally, the study will explore the role of clinical symptoms and the copper chelation status in Wilson's disease in this context.

interventions.name: Collection of SF-12, PSQI, ISI, Epworth, Chalder, PHQ-9, GAD-7, PSS, Flei, and MOCA in Wilson's disease patients at baseline and then every 6 to 12 months thereafter.
